decision: Which parts of our signup flow cost us the most signups, and what should we remove or test first?
limitations: It reads command-line options or one JSON object. Unknown names, stray arguments and flags missing a value stop the run; options you leave out take the defaults shown in --help.
Opportunity figures are capped at the friction-blocked share of non-converters (15% by default) and split by directional B2B SaaS priors. They rank fixes; they don't forecast conversion.
Only the yes/no blocking flags get a monthly value. Extra fields and steps lower the score but don't appear as valued fixes, so a field-heavy flow can show no opportunity.
It scores the form, not the offer or lead quality. Dropping qualifying fields can lift signups while flooding sales with poor leads or lowering activation.
review: Whoever owns the signup flow walks the live flow on a phone to confirm the fields, steps and flags entered, and the sales lead confirms which fields qualification needs. Test one change at a time, measured on signups and activation.
